problem: The [shown output] block after the script is empty. A student sees a blank output panel and cannot tell whether the script prints anything.
fix: Remove the output block, or fill it with: 'No console output. The script prints nothing; the cube moves in the Scene view and the impulse of 1.6 N·s gives 2.0 m/s on a 0.8 kg body.'

problem: 'The engine detects contacts in FixedUpdate' is inaccurate about the order. FixedUpdate runs first, then the physics simulation step, and the collision and trigger callbacks come after the simulation in that same fixed cycle. A student may think contact detection happens inside their FixedUpdate code.
fix: Write: 'The engine simulates physics on each fixed step, after all FixedUpdate calls. It resolves contacts from mass and material properties, updates positions, and then calls OnCollision and OnTrigger callbacks.'

problem: 'Physics.Raycast(origin, direction, out hit, distance, layerMask) returns the first hit' is misleading. The method returns a bool (true if something was hit); the hit details are written into the out parameter hit.
fix: Write: 'Physics.Raycast(origin, direction, out hit, distance, layerMask) returns true if the ray hits a collider, and fills hit (a RaycastHit) with the first hit's point, normal and collider.'

problem: Trigger callbacks need a Rigidbody on at least one of the two objects. The chapter never states this, so a student whose trigger silently does nothing has no clue why.
fix: Add: 'OnTriggerEnter only fires if at least one of the two objects has a Rigidbody; two plain trigger colliders with no Rigidbody report nothing.'

problem: The figure shows the message 'move object' from Script to Display, but section 2 says the physics engine updates positions. The two descriptions of who moves the object disagree.
fix: Change that arrow to Physics → Display with label 'updated transform', or relabel Script → Display as 'render transform'.

problem: The pointer 'see 3D manipulation and travel' is plain text, so it does not work as a chapter link on a phone.
fix: Mark it up as a link to the chapter, e.g. 3D manipulation and travel.
